source_task.title: Research: Agent Token Cost Attribution Guide 2026

key_insights: Agentic coding tasks consume 1000x more tokens than code reasoning or code chat tasks
Input tokens (not output) dominate overall agent cost, even with prompt caching enabled
Token usage is highly stochastic — same task can differ by 30x in total tokens across runs
Higher token consumption does NOT correlate with higher accuracy; accuracy peaks at intermediate cost
Frontier LLMs fail to predict their own token usage (max correlation 0.39), systematically underestimating
Agent runs consume 5-30x more tokens than a single chatbot prompt (Gartner, Mar 2026)
Enterprise AI spend hit $37B in 2025, up from $11.5B year prior
37% of enterprises now run 5+ LLMs in production; top 3 providers = 88% of API usage
EU AI Act Article 12 logging requirements take full effect Aug 2, 2026
Token consumption expected to multiply 24x to 120 quadrillion tokens/month by 2030 (Goldman Sachs)

academic_papers.title: How Do AI Agents Spend Your Money? Analyzing and Predicting Token Consumption in Agentic Coding Tasks
academic_papers.authors: Bai et al. (UMich, Stanford, All Hands AI, Google Deepmind, MIT)
academic_papers.key_finding: First systematic study of agent token consumption; input tokens dominate; 30x variance on same task; no correlation between token usage and accuracy

academic_papers.title: Tokenomics: Quantifying Where Tokens Are Used in Agentic Software Engineering
academic_papers.key_finding: Token distribution analysis in multi-agent systems

vendor_specific_patterns.approach: AI Foundry + APIM gateway + Application Insights with OpenTelemetry + KQL dashboards for per-agent, per-model cost
Prompt caching (cache reads ~10% of base input); output billed 5x input rate; no per-model/project/session breakdown in /usage endpoint

request_tagging: Tag every LLM request with user_id, feature, deployment, prompt_version, agent_run_id, customer_id
Tag at SDK call site (not post-hoc log parsing) to preserve context
Low-cardinality fields for alerting; high-cardinality for drill-down
enforcement: Hard cap per user (at proxy/middleware layer)
Kill switch on agent runs (token count, tool-call count, span depth)
common_mistakes: Not tagging every request (aggregates to unknown)
Stale price tables (vendor pricing changes monthly)
Ignoring cached vs uncached input pricing

market_trends_2026: Prompt caching became a first-class FinOps dimension (OpenAI GA 2024-2025, Anthropic 2025)
Helicone acquired by Mintlify (Mar 2026) → maintenance mode with security updates only
Portkey acquired by Palo Alto Networks (2025) → security-first lineage
OpenInference semantic conventions now cover token and cost attributes
EU AI Act Article 12 audit trail requirements → logging becomes mandatory
Agentic workloads driving 5-30x token consumption vs chatbot prompts
Goldman Sachs forecasts 24x token growth to 120 quadrillion tokens/month by 2030
